decisions.reason: The low-pile decorative carpet sits close to the core offer and costs little to keep listed, and one year of presence does not yet resolve uncertainty about its value, so the option stays open.

The hand-knotted wool silk carpet is a premium piece that fits the firm's craftsmanship positioning, and it is cheap to hold in the collection while demand from projects and private clients becomes clear.
This is another low-pile decorative carpet within a crowded rug range, so some collection pruning is possible, but early evidence does not justify abandoning it yet.
The corner bench extends the established seating and dining offer with low carrying cost and room for customization, so it should be kept while its value unfolds.
The low-pile carpet adds to a broad portfolio of similar options and could later be pruned, but there is not yet enough evidence to drop it.
The swivel shell chair is close to the core upholstery business and likely backed by a designer collaboration, so keeping it preserves its upside at little cost.
